claims.value: Sokoto; Gwandu for the western emirates

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Twin capital at Gwandu; eastern and western emirates; capital district Sokoto
evidence.note: The country study describes the principal caliph at Sokoto and the western administrative capital at Gwandu. This conservative late-century interval precedes British conquest and does not substitute modern Nigerian capitals.

qualifications: Sokoto retained primacy; Gwandu administered the western division. The centres are not flattened into identical roles.
No territorial geometry or statistical scope is inferred.

claims.value: Usman dan Fodio — Islamic scholar and reformer associated with the founding of the Sokoto caliphate

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Radical mallams; jihad beginning in Gobir in 1804; broad religious and political impact
evidence.note: The country study establishes his religious reform movement and historical influence, independently of routine officeholding. The Library of Congress identifies him as the author of a surviving religious manuscript and dates his lifespan.

evidence.locator: Title, Names, Summary and Rights & Access metadata
evidence.note: Catalogue identifies Usuman dan Fodio (1754–1817) as author of a work concerning the authority of Islamic scholars. The broad catalogue publication range is not a dated publication event.

qualifications: His significance rests on religious scholarship, reform and documented broad influence, not merely officeholding.
The manuscript catalogue does not establish a precise composition date; no work is asserted to have appeared by 1815 solely from its catalogue date range.
No disputed date of transfer of administrative power to Muhammad Bello is resolved here.

figure.name: Usman dan Fodio
figure.relationship: Scholar and reformer whose movement founded the Sokoto caliphate; not a back-projected modern Nigerian nationality.
figure.activity: Living founder and religious intellectual relevant to the caliphate in 1815; no assertion of a particular newly published work in that year.
figure.contribution: Islamic reformist scholarship and a movement with major political and religious consequences across the savanna and Sahel.
